title: Affine ind-étale schemes over a separably closed field
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a separably closed field. For a profinite set $S$ let
$LC(S,\Omega)$ be the $\Omega$-algebra of locally constant functions $S\to\Omega$
and $\Omega[S]=\Spec LC(S,\Omega)$.

1. Every étale $\Omega$-algebra of finite presentation is isomorphic to
   $\Omega^n=LC(\{1,\dots,n\},\Omega)$ for some $n\geq0$.
2. Every ind-étale $\Omega$-algebra is isomorphic to $LC(S,\Omega)$ for a
   profinite set $S$, and every $LC(S,\Omega)$ is ind-étale.
3. For profinite $S,T$, the map
   $\operatorname{Cont}(T,S)\to\Hom_{\Omega\text{-alg}}(LC(S,\Omega),LC(T,\Omega))$,
   $s\mapsto(f\mapsto f\circ s)$, is bijective.

Hence $S\mapsto\Omega[S]$ is an equivalence from the category of profinite sets
onto the category of affine ind-étale $\Omega$-schemes. It is the functor
$S\mapsto X[S]$ of [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] for $X=\Spec\Omega$.

proof.text: Use the existing equivalence of a finite etale algebra over a separably closed field with the product indexed by its finite prime spectrum; enumerate that spectrum by Fin n.

Evaluate an ind-etale algebra at each prime using the unique inverse of its separably closed residue-field scalar map. Each element comes from a finite etale stage, proving local constancy. Evaluations separate elements because ind-etale algebras over a field are absolutely flat and reduced. Surjectivity follows from liftPrimeSpectrum and its evaluation congruence. Characteristic functions separate points and show that the spectrum is totally separated, hence profinite.
Locally constant algebras are ind-Zariski by the existing finite-discrete-quotient colimit presentation, hence ind-etale. Canonical ULift transports give the across-universes predicate.

Precomposition is injective since clopen characteristic functions separate points of a profinite space. Given an algebra map use the existing prime-spectrum homeomorphism Spec LC(S, Ω) ≃ S × Spec Ω to construct its continuous map. The vanishing of f minus its value at the resulting point proves that precomposition equals the given map.

Apply the proved categorical assembly lemma: the algebraic Hom bijection and fully faithful relative spectrum functor give full faithfulness, and the algebra classification gives essential surjectivity. For the test-object comparison, construct the pushout LC(S, ℤ) ⊔_ℤ Ω = LC(S, Ω). Characteristic functions of fibres become one after localization at the chosen prime, so a ring map on LC(S, Ω) is determined by its scalar map and its restriction to LC(S, ℤ). liftPrimeSpectrum constructs the unique map with these data. Taking spectra gives precisely the defining base-change pullback. Uniqueness of the pullback comparison gives an isomorphism over Spec Ω; the two projection equations prove naturality.
